title: Coordinate-ring comparisons for one affine triple
statement: Let $I,D,c,S,i_0,X_0,Y_0,f_0,g_0,W,V,U$ have the following properties: $I$ is a directed preordered set; $D:I^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Scheme}$ has affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism]; $c$ is a limiting cone with apex $S$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; $i_0\in I$; $X_0,Y_0$ are schemes over $S_{i_0}$ [def-pc-scheme]; $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ is a morphism over $S_{i_0}$ locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; $g_0:Y_0\to S_{i_0}$ is the structure map; and $W\subseteq S_{i_0},V\subseteq Y_0,U\subseteq X_0$ are affine opens with $V\subseteq g_0^{-1}(W)$ and $U\subseteq f_0^{-1}(V)$. Put $J=\{i\in I\mid i_0\le i\}$ and $o=(i_0,i_0\le i_0)$. For a scheme $T\to S_{i_0}$ write $f_T:X_T\to Y_T$ for the base change of $f_0$ and $U_T\subseteq X_T$ for the inverse image of $U$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. There exist a functor $F:J\to\mathrm{CommRing}$, commutative $F(o)$-algebras $B,C$, and a homomorphism $\varphi:B\to C$ of $F(o)$-algebras of finite presentation (a quotient of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables by a finitely generated ideal), such that: (1) $U_S\to Y_S$ is étale [def-weil-etale-morphism] if and only if the spectrum morphism induced by $\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{colim}F}\otimes\varphi$ is étale, with the $F(o)$-algebra structure on $\operatorname{colim}F$ induced by its coprojection; (2) for every $i\in J$, if the spectrum morphism induced by $\mathrm{id}_{F(i)}\otimes\varphi$ is étale, then $U_{S_i}\to Y_{S_i}$ is étale, with $F(i)$ regarded as an $F(o)$-algebra via $F(o\to i)$. Here tensor products are over $F(o)$, and spectrum reverses ring maps. No étaleness hypothesis or existence of an étale stage is assumed or asserted.

proof.text: For i in J let Wᵢ be the inverse image of W in Sᵢ. Affineness of transition maps makes every Wᵢ affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Restricted transition maps make the coordinate rings F(i)=Γ(Wᵢ) a covariant functor. Identify F(o) with Γ(W) using D.map(id)=id and the induced identification Wₒ=W. Take B=Γ(V), C=Γ(U), with their F(o)-algebra structures from the structure maps. The map φ is induced by the restriction of f₀; its compatibility with the base algebra follows from f₀ being a morphism over Sᵢ₀. It is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation].

The opens diagram over i₀ is equivalent to the upper-tail inverse system. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-cone-affine-projections-opens] its restricted cone with apex W_S is limiting. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit], Spec(colim F) is another limit with the coprojection legs. The unique comparison isomorphism identifies W_S with Spec(colim F), compatibly with the projections and especially its map to W. Thus its Γ(W)-algebra structure agrees with the coprojection F(o)→colim F.

For T=S or Sᵢ, let W_T be the inverse image of W. The equality of structure morphisms and U⊆f₀⁻¹(V), V⊆g₀⁻¹(W) show that the inverse image of U in X_T is also the intersection of that inverse image with the inverse image of W_T. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] it is U×_W W_T. Likewise the inverse image of V is V×_W W_T. Under the affine spectrum identifications and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], these are Spec(A_T⊗C) and Spec(A_T⊗B), with A_T=F(i) or colim F. The restricted map is Spec(id⊗φ): both morphisms have the same projections, since id⊗φ sends 1⊗b to 1⊗φ(b) and a⊗1 to a⊗1. Pullback uniqueness identifies the maps.

The map from the source chart into Y_T is the restricted affine map followed by the open inclusion of the target chart. That inclusion is étale, so composition and cancellation in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] give an equivalence between their étaleness. Isomorphisms preserve étaleness. Apply the identifications of the preceding step to obtain clause (1) and, taking the forward implication from ring-model étaleness, clause (2).
